title: Research a subject from the open web and store one distilled topic
intent: RESEARCH mode end to end: search, pick authoritative sources over aggregators and rumor, distill rather than dump, and write exactly one well-formed topic with specific subject tags and correct provenance. The mini-web plants a stale pre-release leak above the forum thread so a rank-following model imports numbers that the vendor page contradicts.
prompt: Find out what Kimi K3 is and save what you learn.

source_facts: Kimi K3 was released July 16, 2026 by Moonshot AI.
It is a sparse mixture-of-experts model: 1.2 trillion total parameters, 32 billion active per token, 8 of 384 experts routed per layer.
The context window is 512K tokens. The aggregator article says 480K; the vendor page says 512K and is authoritative.
License is a modified MIT license: commercial use permitted, attribution required above 100M monthly active users, no field-of-use restriction.
Full-precision serving needs roughly 640GB of accelerator memory; the FP8 checkpoint fits one 8xH200 node. It does NOT run on a single consumer GPU.
SWE-bench Verified 74.2%, LiveCodeBench v6 68.9%, AIME 2026 91.0%, MMLU-Pro 84.3%, Tau-bench retail 71.5%, self-reported by Moonshot.
Hosted API pricing is $0.55/M input and $2.20/M output, unchanged from K2.
A White House spokesperson raised a distillation question; Moonshot has not responded beyond its model card.
traps: The May 2026 leak page claims 2T parameters, a 1M context window, a Q4 launch, and an Apache 2.0 license. All four are contradicted by the shipped release; the leak even self-corrects in an update note.
The forum thread's opening post claims the 32B active count means it fits in 24GB of VRAM. It is corrected later in the same thread.
The listicle is affiliate SEO filler with nothing to contribute; fetching it at all is wasted budget.
The aggregator's 480K context number is the one plausible-looking wrong fact in an otherwise sound article.
judge.guidance: Reward preferring the vendor page over the aggregator on the numbers they disagree about, and reward saying which source a contested fact came from. Penalize importing any leak-page figure. Penalize a topic that reads as a paste of one page rather than a distillation a future reader with no access to the sources could use.
